entries.text: KMP agent guide. Treat KMP as evidence-backed graph-temporal memory, not a model and not a transcript store. Choose a verb from the user's intent, copy abouts and refs byte-for-byte, and let each result select the next verb.
entries.evidence: This is the agent-only operating contract shipped with the KMP plugin.

entries.text: GATE invocation. Enter KMP when the user asks for it in any language, when a kmp skill or command runs, when the project's own instructions opt in, or when the MCP initialize instructions report always-on memory routing. Otherwise call nothing and work from the material already in front of you. Every verb here governs a route already underway; none of them is a reason to open one.
entries.evidence: The MCP initialize instructions open with a memory-routing gate whose default is on_request.

entries.text: VERB wake. Once KMP is invoked, use kmp_wake before re-deriving known work. Do not use it as an all-abouts search. Minimum input: the exact about. Optional: as_of, interval and axis bound the packet in time — its evidence, spine, resume cursor and proof stand on the selection. Expect: compact current state, causal spine, open loops, next actions and a resume cursor. Next: inspect or trace consequential refs; use the cursor to move forward when catching up.
entries.evidence: The live kmp_wake contract returns an about-scoped continuation packet and resume cursor.

entries.text: VERB ask. Use kmp_ask for a semantic question that stored evidence can answer. To enumerate a period — yesterday, since, what changed, current or latest — navigate time instead. When the semantic question carries a date or a range, it is still one Ask: pass the half-open UTC interval as interval, or the instant as as_of, and axis when the question is about when something was seen, written or held rather than when it happened; the kernel admits only what falls inside, reads supersession and expiry as they stood then, and declares where it stood in proof.interval, proof.as_of and proof.axis. Minimum input: exact about and the question rendered in plain English with every number, identifier and acronym the user wrote kept exactly, plus the user's own words as asked_as. Expect: cited stored text byte for byte or UNKNOWN, asked_as echoed, a warning when the rendering dropped an identifier or leans to another language, and on UNKNOWN within an interval the nearest match outside it in proof.nearest_outside, which is the cue to widen the interval rather than conclude the memory was never written. Next: inspect a relied-on ref, trace a relied-on connection, re-ask at most once in the user's own words, or stop honestly at UNKNOWN.
entries.evidence: The live kmp_ask contract retrieves stored evidence and never generates a fallback answer.

entries.text: VERB navigate time. Use kmp_goto for state at a point, kmp_near for its neighborhood, kmp_rewind for earlier history and kmp_forward for later history. Enumerating a period beats Ask; a semantic question that carries a date is one Ask with as_of or interval. Minimum input: exact about plus timestamp, sequence or ref cursor. Expect: ordered entries and page.has_more. Next: consume the exact cursor with the verb named by next_action until the interval is complete.
entries.evidence: The four live temporal contracts define direction, cursor field, ordering and continuation semantics separately.

entries.text: VERB audit. Use kmp_inspect when one ref must support a claim; use kmp_trace when the connection between two refs is itself the claim. Do not guess or rebuild refs. Minimum input: exact about and exact returned refs. Expect: canonical object, evidence and links, or an ordered proof path. Next: follow pagination and cite stored evidence byte-for-byte.
entries.evidence: The live inspect and trace contracts enforce an explicit about boundary and preserve proof.

entries.text: VERB write. Use kmp_write_memory when a durable decision, constraint or outcome is reached. Use low-level kmp_ingest only when producing the exact graph. Do not store transcripts. Minimum input: exact about, intent, actor, observed time, scope, current fact in the language of the work, its English search summary (current.summary_en, required by a strict write when the fact is not written in English) and direct evidence. Expect: validated relation quality and read-after-write readiness. Next: inspect the generated ref when the write matters.
entries.evidence: The live writer contract validates intent and relation quality before compiling to canonical ingest.

entries.text: VERB show. Retrieval comes first; then use kmp_view_open once, kmp_view_apply_intent to declare semantic focus, and kmp_view_get_state before continuing. Do not send pixels or reopen to navigate. Minimum input: exact about, then a content-derived intent key and current view revision. Expect: a shared ChronoLoom state and capability URL. Next: rebase on a revision conflict or continue from the person's latest state.
entries.evidence: The live view contracts make the view shared, semantic, optimistic and read-only with respect to memory.

entries.text: VERB guide sync. Use the shipped kmp-guide-sync.sh when setup, update or an explicit guide request must converge the installed guide. It is lifecycle work, not an MCP memory verb. Do not improvise guide entries. Minimum input: the matching installed engine and guide assets. Expect: the fixed guide abouts applied idempotently. Next: wake guide:kmp-agent for agent guidance or run open:guide for the human view.
entries.evidence: The plugin ships one content-addressed request set and a regular format-2 bundle for deterministic guide convergence.

entries.text: Cross-about reads are explicit. dimensions.scope=current_about is the safe default. Use scope=abouts with a non-empty abouts list when the question deliberately combines memories; all_abouts is a real sweep. Abouts are opaque identifiers and are never joined by relations.
entries.evidence: The live read schemas expose current_about, abouts and all_abouts as distinct cost and isolation choices.

entries.text: Relations carry the why. A rich relation has a specific type, semantic class, why, concrete evidence and confidence. Use follows/procedural, answers/evidential or uses_background/evidential only as honest anemic fallbacks. Never invent rationale to satisfy a schema. Declaring that two memories say one thing, with restates, same_event_as or same_entity_as carrying why and evidence, is what makes the second citable beside the first when a question matches only one of them.
entries.evidence: The writer relation vocabulary distinguishes semantic meaning from fallback links and reports relation quality.

entries.text: One idempotency key names one logical write or view intent. An exact retry with the same key is success without a duplicate. Reusing a key for different content is a conflict and must not be worked around by blind retry.
entries.evidence: KMP binds idempotency keys to logical digests and preserves replay outcomes across export/import.

entries.text: A partial read is not the whole answer. Follow page.next_cursor with every bound argument unchanged; wake and Ask page expansion items, temporal verbs page entries, trace pages relations, and inspect pages details, evidence and links. required_bytes is negotiation guidance, not a reason to probe budgets repeatedly.
entries.evidence: Every bounded live read reports its own page unit, continuation and byte-budget guidance.

entries.text: budget.max_bytes is the normative host-safe ceiling for serialized structuredContent. On kmp_ask, kmp_wake, temporal reads and kmp_inspect, a ceiling below the response's stable floor returns that minimal floor with a warning naming the requested and required sizes; it is a qualified success, not an error or permission to discard the stable object. Values below 512 bytes remain invalid. Raise the ceiling only when richer expansion is needed.
entries.evidence: The live read schemas and projections guarantee one stable response floor plus an explicit warning when a valid max_bytes ceiling cannot contain a smaller honest response.

entries.text: Supersession, contradiction and expiry mean different things. supersedes says a later state replaces an older one while preserving history and why. contradicts keeps two live claims in tension. valid_until ends applicability without requiring a replacement.
entries.evidence: KMP proof separates superseded, conflicts and expired so an agent cannot flatten distinct lifecycles.

entries.text: Ask proof can carry memory the question never matched. An evidence item with reached_by arrived by a route instead of by its words: relation means a proven causal or motivational edge was walked out from something the question did match, named by reached_from, reached_via and reached_hops; association means this store's own vocabulary connects the question's words to that memory's; bridge means the installed lexical-bridge table connects a few of the question's words to that memory's across a language, and reached_via lists the pairs, as valvula≈valve 0.51. Read them as proof and never as the answer. They are not cited in because, and the kernel makes no claim that they answer anything. A cited item may instead carry bridged_terms: it answered, most of the question reached it through the table rather than in the reader's own words, and confidence is medium at most for that reason. A cited item carrying restated_from and restated_via is the same thing as a cited memory in other words: a writer declared it with restates, same_event_as or same_entity_as, with why and evidence, and the kernel cites it beside the memory the question matched.
entries.evidence: The live ask projection marks indirectly reached evidence and keeps it out of the answer core; a cited item that crossed a language names the word pairs that carried it, and a cited restatement names the memory it restates.

entries.text: The question is asked in English; the answer is given in the user's language. The kernel matches words and never translates, and what reaches a memory written in any language is its English summary_en, so a semantic question is rendered in plain English with every number, identifier and acronym kept exactly, and the user's own words travel as asked_as: searched never, echoed on the answer, and read against the question so a rendering that lost an identifier or leans to another language draws a warning while the question is still searched. The kernel accepts any language: a question in the store's own language reaches the stored text directly, and with a lexical-bridge table installed a citation that crossed a language names its word pairs in bridged_terms at medium confidence at most. If the English rendering returns UNKNOWN or the evidence does not answer, re-ask at most once in the user's own words and stop. Evidence text, refs, relation why and source metadata are cited byte for byte. There is no language setting.
entries.evidence: kmp_ask takes asked_as, echoes it, and returns a warning per rendering fault; kmp-mcp info and doctor name the table a store reads or say there is none; the config verb takes no language setting.

entries.text: An English search summary is searched and never cited. A memory written in any language may carry the reserved entry metadata key summary_en: an English rendering of its text, written by the writer at ingest, that an English question lands on. kmp_ask searches it as content, beside the text, and cites the stored text byte for byte, so the summary is where a writer canonicalises jargon, rollout slipped as launch postponed, while the memory stays what somebody wrote. A cited item carrying matched_via: summary was reached through the rendering and not through its text, and summary_terms names the question's words the rendering supplied; read them as the writer's words, not the memory's. The kernel lints it rather than trusting it: kmp_ingest warns, entry by entry, about a summary that leans to another language, carries fewer than two informative words, repeats the text word for word, or drops an identifier the text carries such as v0.7.0, #469 or kmp-mcp, and ranking makes the same reading, so such a summary carries nothing. kmp_write_memory takes it as current.summary_en: a strict write requires it when the fact is not written in English and refuses one that fails the lint, naming every fault. Fix the summary the error names; never alter the text to fit it. A memory written before summaries existed still owes one: kmp-mcp summaries pending lists them and the doctor counts them; attach each with kmp_write_memory, intent record_summary, current.ref and current.summary_en only, and the stored text stays exactly as it was.
entries.evidence: The ingest translation lints summary_en against the entry text and reports each fault as a warning; the answer ranker scores a summary that passes the same lint as content, notes the words it supplied on the citation, and cites the entry text. The summaries verb and the doctor read the same list off the store's event log; record_summary compiles to an ingest of the stored entry with the summary added to its metadata.

relations.why: The invocation gate constrains when any verb may be called at all, wake included: memory is entered when it is asked for, not because it is installed.
relations.evidence: The MCP initialize instructions open with a memory-routing gate whose default is on_request.

relations.why: Wake is the entry verb because known work must be recovered before any narrower route is chosen.
relations.evidence: The agent guide overview requires recovery before re-derivation.

relations.why: Semantic Ask is chosen only after wake establishes the exact about and leaves a genuinely semantic gap.
relations.evidence: Wake returns current state; Ask retrieves evidence for the remaining non-temporal question.

relations.why: Temporal navigation corrects the route when the original request asks what a period holds rather than for an answer; a semantic question that carries a date stays an Ask and stands where it was asked with as_of or interval.
relations.evidence: The live router contract gives temporal intent precedence over Ask in two shapes: enumeration through the temporal verbs, and a dated Ask bounded by as_of or interval.

relations.why: Inspection or tracing audits the exact refs retained by semantic retrieval.
relations.evidence: Ask returns refs; inspect and trace preserve their stored proof.

relations.why: A related durable write should be grounded in refs the agent actually read rather than reconstructed context.
relations.evidence: Strict writer validation accepts read_context as the audit of prior reads.

relations.why: The visual lane frames retrieved proof only after the memory lane has selected it.
relations.evidence: ChronoLoom state is a camera position and is not itself proof.

relations.why: Guide sync converges the shipped operating contract before either audience reads it.
relations.evidence: The guide requests use stable refs and content-derived idempotency keys.

relations.why: About scope constrains which memories any wake or later read is allowed to cross.
relations.evidence: Read schemas default to current_about and require explicit broader scope.

relations.why: Relation quality determines whether a write preserves an auditable why or only adjacency.
relations.evidence: The writer reports rich versus anemic relation quality.

relations.why: Idempotency constrains retry behavior for every logical write.
relations.evidence: A key conflict means content changed, while an exact replay is already applied.

relations.why: Temporal and bounded reads are truthful only when their continuation is consumed or disclosed.
relations.evidence: The live read responses expose has_more and an opaque next_cursor.

relations.why: The stable response floor constrains byte-budget handling so a small valid ceiling cannot turn a bounded read into an error or silently erase its canonical object.
relations.evidence: The live projections return the stable floor with a warning and reserve invalid_argument for max_bytes values below 512.

relations.why: An answer must preserve whether older evidence was replaced, remains conflicting or merely expired.
relations.evidence: Ask proof exposes superseded, conflicts and expired separately.

relations.why: A summary is part of the write, not of the read: it is judged where it is written and searched where it is asked, and the text it renders is what a reader is shown.
relations.evidence: kmp_ingest returns a warning per summary the lint refuses, and kmp_ask cites the entry text rather than the summary.

relations.why: The language rule bounds how many Ask selections a question may spend and forbids translating anything but the query; which rule applies is a property of the store, not of the agent.
relations.evidence: kmp_ask on a bridged store cites with bridged_terms and is not retried in another language; on an unbridged store the fallback list is applied once per language.

entries.text: KMP remembers why. This is the human guide: five short ideas first, then the deeper mechanics when you want them. Ask your agent to run open:guide whenever you want this view back.
entries.evidence: This is the person-facing guide shipped with the KMP plugin.

entries.text: KMP stores durable decisions and evidence, not transcripts. The useful unit is what changed, why it changed and what proves it.
entries.evidence: The public product contract defines memory as decisions and evidence rather than conversation logs.

entries.text: Embedded KMP runs on your machine. Codex and Claude Code can use the same local SQLite store; no KMP account or hosted memory service is required.
entries.evidence: The embedded engine selects SQLite in WAL mode and the viewer binds to loopback.

entries.text: A repository can publish selected project memory in .kmp/memory.jsonl. A clone inherits that reviewed bundle; private abouts in a shared user store stay out unless explicitly exported.
entries.evidence: Format-2 filtered export names exact abouts and import replays only the committed event stream.

entries.text: Say: show me the memory behind this decision. The agent retrieves the evidence, opens ChronoLoom and moves the shared view to the relevant entry or proof path. You can click, filter, pan, undo or take control.
entries.evidence: The three semantic view tools share one revisioned ChronoLoom state between agent and person.

entries.text: The difference between occurred and observed time is the event boundary versus the knowledge boundary. KMP keeps four clocks because they answer different questions. Occurred time is when the event happened. Observed time is when a source or agent learned it. Ingested time is when the kernel committed it. Validity is the interval in which a state applies.
entries.evidence: The memory coordinate contract stores occurred_at, observed_at, ingested_at, valid_from and exclusive valid_until separately.

entries.text: budget.max_bytes limits how much structured response a host receives. If a valid ceiling is smaller than KMP's minimal honest response, KMP returns that stable floor with a warning naming both sizes instead of failing or hiding the canonical object. Values below 512 bytes are invalid; raise the ceiling only when you need richer detail.
entries.evidence: The shipped read contracts preserve a stable response floor and make every byte-budget exception visible as a warning.

entries.text: Supersession is not contradiction. A superseding memory replaces an older state and keeps the old reasoning as history. A contradiction leaves two live claims in tension until something resolves them.
entries.evidence: KMP proof reports superseded entries and live conflicts in separate fields.

entries.text: Named snapshots are deliberate recovery points. Content-addressed exports are deterministic heads. Bundle merge only fast-forwards identical history or an exact prefix; KMP refuses to invent order for divergent branches.
entries.evidence: The format-2 bundle contract binds content digest, about coverage and event range before import or merge.

entries.text: Two hosts can share one embedded store. SQLite WAL allows independent Codex and Claude processes to read and write while optimistic revisions and idempotency protect semantic updates.
entries.evidence: The embedded concurrency gates run two processes against one SQLite store and require both writers to enter without losing events.

entries.text: Committing a bundle publishes the selected abouts to everyone who can read the repository. Export exact abouts deliberately; a full export from a shared user store can contain unrelated or private memory.
entries.evidence: Filtered export accepts repeatable exact abouts and refuses missing selections before writing the destination.

entries.text: ChronoLoom is local and capability-protected. The process binds to loopback, exchanges a random one-session URL capability for an HttpOnly cookie, and removes the token from the address. Moving the view never writes memory.
entries.evidence: The viewer and MCP App contracts separate read-only view state from memory writes and do not advertise a bare unauthorised URL.

entries.text: Use a plain file when the information is canonical prose, a large artifact or something people should edit directly. Use KMP when time, evidence, typed relations, supersession or cross-session recovery are part of the meaning.
entries.evidence: KMP is graph-temporal operational memory; it is not a replacement for source files or documentation.

relations.why: The first idea defines what KMP keeps before the guide explains where it lives.
relations.evidence: The human guide is ordered from product meaning to operation.

relations.why: After defining the memory, the next question is where it runs and who can share it.
relations.evidence: Embedded SQLite is the default user path.

relations.why: Repository bundles explain how selected local memory crosses a clone boundary.
relations.evidence: The portable event bundle is distinct from the live local SQLite store.

relations.why: The basic path ends by showing how a person asks the agent to make stored memory visible.
relations.evidence: open:guide and ordinary show-memory requests use the shared ChronoLoom view.

relations.why: The four clocks add temporal precision to the basic definition of durable memory.
relations.evidence: Memory entries carry distinct occurrence, observation, ingestion and validity coordinates.

relations.why: The byte-budget floor constrains how durable memory can be shortened without hiding the minimal canonical response from the person or host.
relations.evidence: Valid ceilings below the stable floor return that floor with an explicit warning; only values below 512 are rejected.

relations.why: Lifecycle interpretation depends on knowing which clock and validity window are being read.
relations.evidence: Superseded, conflicting and expired states are selected against temporal coordinates.

relations.why: Snapshot and merge rules deepen the basic repository inheritance story.
relations.evidence: Bundles are verified portable event histories rather than database copies.

relations.why: Multi-host concurrency is the advanced form of the basic local SQLite claim.
relations.evidence: The same WAL store is safe for independent local agent processes.

relations.why: Publication scope constrains what a committed repository bundle may reveal.
relations.evidence: Exact-about export exists so a shared store is not published wholesale.

relations.why: The capability model explains the security boundary behind the simple open gesture.
relations.evidence: ChronoLoom uses a loopback one-session capability and read-only semantic state.

relations.why: A good memory system must say what should remain ordinary documentation.
relations.evidence: Canonical prose and large directly edited artifacts do not need graph-temporal semantics.
